provenance.built_from: the source text only — Dickens, A Christmas Carol (PG #46), as sliced by src/extraction/sources.ts. Line numbers below are into that slice.
provenance.blind_to: candidate output. No segmentation or extraction run was consulted while building this file, per §3.1's rule that an alignment decision is recorded, not reverse-engineered.
provenance.author: hand-annotated

included_when: the source states something concrete at the plant scene — an object, a rule, a promise, a capability or a relationship, not a mood
a later scene depends on it, such that removing the plant would change how that later scene reads
a reader could name both ends without being shown this file
excluded: ordinary continuity — a character still being where the last scene left them
facts the story asserts and never collects
pairs whose plant and payoff fall in the same scene
inclusion_rule.note: This records pairs a reader would name. It is NOT a claim about ADR 0020's trigger term, and it adds no pays_off edges to the package. Several plants pay off more than once; each payoff is its own row, because §3.7 scores {fact_ref, plant, payoff} triples.

implicit.why: "Are there no prisons?" asked Scrooge (l.287); the Spirit turns the same words on him at Ignorance and Want (l.2736). The longest-range verbatim callback in the story.
implicit.span_note: 10 scenes — the long-range case §3.7's second bar exists for.

implicit.why: "You will be haunted... by Three Spirits" (l.861) is the promise the entire middle of the book discharges; the first arrival is its first collection.
The third spirit arrives as foretold. Same plant, a second payoff — the structure §3.7 scores per triple.
"I wear the chain I forged in life" (l.740), made "of my own free will" (l.742). The grave is what Scrooge's own chain has been earning, and why he can still refuse it.
The invitation refused in the first scene is the invitation accepted in the second-to-last. The reform is measured against it.
Scrooge meets the same gentleman, apologises, and whispers a sum — the refusal in scene 1 is what makes the whisper land.
"I'll raise your salary" (l.3781) collects the fifteen shillings and the grudged Christmas Day from the opening scene.

The Spirit's "a crutch without an owner, carefully preserved" (l.2229) is the exact image the later Cratchit scene realises. Distinct from tiny_tims_fate_uncertain: this is the object, not the prognosis.
Scrooge's own argument that the power to make people happy or unhappy "costs so little" is the model he becomes as a master.
"I should like to be able to say a word or two to my clerk just now" (l.1520) — said watching Fezziwig, collected across fifteen scenes in the office.
Belle's "Another idol has displaced me" (l.1543) names the gain that the neglected grave is the end state of.
The disagreeable animal is Uncle Scrooge (l.2642), guessed by a party he is not at; the payoff is his arriving at that same party in person.
The bed-curtains, blankets and shirt sold at Old Joe's are what the bare, plundered room is missing. The shop scene is what makes the empty room legible.
Scrooge asks the Spirit for any tenderness connected with a death; the relief of Caroline and her husband is the answer, and the stone is where it lands.
"Doom" written on Ignorance's brow, unless the writing be erased, is the conditional the whole Stave IV sequence tests and the graveyard states.
